result_summary: A per-DocDistance embed memo keyed on (resolved path, mtime, size, segmentation kwargs) cuts the shipped 55-row --pairs batch from a median 11.032 s to 1.110 s, 9.94x against a 3x bar, with segment-and-encode calls falling 110 to 11 (90% skipped) and 99 cache hits. Every emitted byte is unchanged: 9 of 9 arms produce byte-identical JSONL, the 55 per-pair --details-json files match on all 3 repeats, and the end-to-end CliRunner run of distance-semantic --pairs gives the same sha256 under both arms, so V stays 0/24, the 55 default-path smd and order_gap values are np.array_equal across arms, and the metric property is untouched (identity 0.0, symmetry 2.2e-16, 0/495 triangle violations). The worst case costs nothing measurable: on a zero-hit disjoint-pairs control of 110 unique files the memo pays 17.50 ms of key construction over 110 slots, 0.10% of the batch, and wall time moves -0.63%, inside the run-to-run spread and well under the 2% ceiling. The saving tracks the reusable slot fraction rather than row count, so 1-source-x-N returns 1.81x at N=2, 3.24x at N=5 and 5.18x at N=11, and end to end with the 13.5 s model load included the same sweep runs 1.98x.
caveats: Batch wall time excludes the model load, which is the correct comparison for the loop but flatters the deployment figure; the end-to-end CliRunner number including the 13.5 s load is 1.98x and is reported alongside. Timings are wall-clock on a machine running this notebook alone, with the 1-minute load average checked before each of the 56 timed runs (min 5.97, median 7.26, max 7.97, ceiling 8.0, zero breaches); the ceiling forced idle gaps between runs, which quiets each measurement but does not remove the platform dependence of the ratio. The disjoint-pairs control is a generated corpus of 110 documents assembled from the fixture's own 30 paragraphs, since the project holds no natural set of 110 distinct documents; it matches the fixture on size (2565 vs 2359 mean bytes) but segments to more statements, which is why its uncached batch is 17.9 s rather than 11.0 s. A two-row sweep does not clear 3x (1-source-x2 reads 1.81x), so the bar's speedup clause is specific to sweeps with a high reusable-slot fraction. Cache memory grows without bound in the number of distinct documents per instance and was not measured; a shipping memo needs a size bound. The memo does not reach distance-wrt-source, whose reranker and NLI work is per-pair, and one-shot convenience functions build a fresh instance per call so they are unaffected. Nothing under src/ was changed - the memo is a class-level monkeypatch inside the notebook and ships only if this Promoted verdict is acted on in a follow-up.
